::: {.why}
A point-in-time claim you have not tested is a comment, and comments do not stop you from reading the future.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Write a test that fails if any query returns a row whose ingested_at is after the as-of date.
- Say what your store would have returned on 12 March 2019, and demonstrate it rather than assert it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Add `as_of` to the store's query interface, defaulting to now, and make every read filter on ingested_at less than or equal to it. Then write tests/test_asof.py with two tests: one that inserts a row with a future ingested_at and asserts it is invisible, and one that reproduces the store's state on a past date and asserts a known row count.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Write qlib/ingest.py's rebuild path: drop, recreate, ingest, verify row counts, in one command. Time it and put the number in the README. A store you are afraid to rebuild is a store you will stop trusting.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The as-of semantics are now enforced by two tests rather than by intention. This is the first instance of the pattern that week 23 generalises: leakage is prevented by construction and asserted by a test, never by remembering to be careful.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Describe the test that would fail if someone added a query path that ignored as_of. If your suite does not have one, you have not finished.
:::
